explained_differences: TShark links response 9 to query 7 and reports 20ms. The analyzer retains queries 7 and 8 as ambiguous and publishes no latency.
Query 6 has no response; only the analyzer's 5-second observation window gives no_response_observed.
TShark links 1 to 2 with -100ms. The analyzer discards all timing events on timestamp regression and retains only query/response counts.
The analyzer records response 3 as additional_response in query 1's window; TShark publishes no response_to or time for this extra response.

Only the analyzer labels response 8 unmatched and query 9 window_incomplete. Fragment 10, captured-short DNS 11 and incomplete DNS header 12 remain excluded even if TShark extracts partial DNS fields.
TShark links response 2 at 5s+1ns to query 1. The analyzer's closed 5s window has expired: no_response_observed plus unmatched_response; query 3 starts a new window and matches response 4 in 1ns.
TShark links 5 to 6 with 1s; later query 7 reuses the key within the analyzer's window, so the analyzer retracts latency and marks the whole group ambiguous.
